body: Super Monkey Ball 2 is Amusement Vision's GameCube sequel about guiding a monkey inside a transparent ball through suspended obstacle courses. Tilting the stage changes the direction and momentum of the ball, turning a narrow path or moving platform into a test of control. A new story follows AiAi and friends after Dr. Bad-Boon steals their bananas. Its ten worlds organise increasingly elaborate constructions around a simple action: change the slope, observe what the ball does and adjust before it reaches the edge.

Switches alter moving platforms by changing their speed or stopping them, adding timing puzzles to the work of steering. Loops, corkscrews and rotating structures give momentum another purpose beyond making the ball faster. Story mode allows the stages within a world to be attempted in different orders, leaving room to set aside a difficult obstacle and return with another success behind the player. Challenge mode instead preserves the pressure of a more structured sequence, with limited lives and further stages waiting for sufficiently strong performances.

Twelve party games include expanded versions of racing, fighting, target landing, bowling and golf alongside new activities. They turn the same small cast into a substantial local multiplayer collection, making the ball useful in several very different sporting contests. Toshihiro Nagoshi directed the sequel, released in 2002. Its variety depends on the economy of the original idea: a readily understood character and a clear physical object can support a demanding solo obstacle course or an immediately sociable game once the surrounding rules are changed.
